summary: A roundup of NFL Week 13 results from Sunday, December 3, 2023. The San Francisco 49ers beat the Philadelphia Eagles 42-19 in an NFC championship rematch marked by two ejections, while the Detroit Lions reached 9-3 for the first time since 1962 and the New England Patriots were shut out at home again. Other results cover the Dolphins, Falcons, Rams, Cardinals, Texans, Colts and Buccaneers.
one_line: NFL Week 13 roundup: 49ers beat Eagles 42-19, Lions reach 9-3 for first time since 1962, and Patriots are shut out by Chargers 6-0.
key_facts: Brock Purdy threw for 314 yards and four touchdowns and Deebo Samuel scored three TDs as the San Francisco 49ers beat the Philadelphia Eagles 42-19; the 49ers scored touchdowns on six straight possessions.
49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw was ejected after reaching over two officials to touch Eagles chief security officer Dom DiSandro's face with a closed fist; DiSandro was also told to leave.

Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was checked for a concussion, returned with about 10 minutes left, and finished 26-of-45 for 298 yards; the Eagles fell to 10-2 and took their first home loss of the season.
The Los Angeles Chargers beat the New England Patriots 6-0 on two 38-yard Cameron Dicker field goals, their first shutout in six years; the Patriots (2-10) lost their fifth straight game.
New England benched Mac Jones for Bailey Zappe, who was sacked five times (two by Khalil Mack), and the Patriots were shut out at home twice in a season for the first time in franchise history.
The Detroit Lions beat the New Orleans Saints 33-28 to reach 9-3, their best record through 12 games since going 10-2 in 1962; Sam LaPorta had career highs of nine catches for 140 yards.
Saints quarterback Derek Carr left in the fourth quarter with back, shoulder and head injuries after a penalized hit by Bruce Irvin; New Orleans fell to 5-7.
Tyreek Hill had two touchdowns and 157 receiving yards as the Miami Dolphins routed the Washington Commanders 45-15, going 9-3 for the first time since 2001.
The Houston Texans beat the Denver Broncos 22-17 when Jimmie Ward intercepted Russell Wilson in the end zone with nine seconds left; Nico Collins had a career-high 191 receiving yards.
The Indianapolis Colts beat the Tennessee Titans 31-28 in overtime on a four-yard Gardner Minshew pass to Michael Pittman with 2:31 left, for their fourth straight win.
Puka Nacua became the first Rams rookie wide receiver to reach 1,000 yards in a season as the Los Angeles Rams beat the Cleveland Browns 36-19; Joe Flacco made his Browns debut.
Tampa Bay's Mike Evans joined Jerry Rice as the only players with 10 consecutive 1,000-yard receiving seasons in a 21-18 win over Carolina, in Chris Tabor's debut as Panthers interim coach.
The Atlanta Falcons beat the New York Jets 13-8 to take sole possession of first place in the NFC South at 6-6.
The Green Bay Packers beat the defending Super Bowl champion Kansas City Chiefs 27-19 for their fourth win in five games, moving to 6-6.
